title: Wren and the Colony
premise: Gideon Vasquez has spent eleven years alone tending the Verdance, a terraformed garden and beacon station orbiting a dead world, her only companions the plants she grows for colonists still frozen in the ships above. When a distress signal arrives in Old Meridian—a language extinct since the Collapse—she traces it to a second cryo-ark hidden in the system's outer dark, carrying half of humanity's survivors that the ruling Conclave erased from all records. The Conclave's enforcer arrives to silence her, forcing Gideon to choose between obeying the law that kept her safe and waking ten thousand people the law condemned. In the end, Gideon broadcasts the truth to both arks, sacrifices the Verdance to shield the second ship's descent, and wakes to a new colony where justice, not the Conclave, decides who inherits the world.
about_author: Freya Brightwater is a former botanist who spent three years cataloguing seed banks in remote research stations before turning to fiction full-time. She writes science fiction about solitude, stewardship, and the quiet heroism of people systems forget.

chapters.title: The Gardener's Hours
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. Establishes her solitary routine aboard the Verdance: pruning, soil chemistry, logging the beacon pulse nobody answers. Emotional beat: contentment shadowed by loneliness; she talks to plants because no one else listens.

chapters.title: Signal in a Dead Tongue
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. A fragmentary distress signal arrives in Old Meridian, which Gideon knows only from her grandmother's songs. She verifies it isn't an echo or ghost transmission. Emotional beat: wonder curdling into dread—someone out there is alive and shouldn't be.

chapters.title: Inventory of Ghosts
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. She decrypts coordinates buried in the signal using archived Conclave keys she was never meant to access. Teaser of a second ark, the Perpetua, listed as lost two centuries ago. Emotional beat: the thrill of discovery laced with guilt at trespassing.

chapters.title: What the Beacon Was For
chapters.summary: Flashback chapter, Gideon's POV. Her recruitment by the Conclave's Terraforming Office and the strange condition of her posting: maintain the beacon, ask no questions about its origin. Emotional beat: retroactive unease as old instructions begin reading like warnings.

chapters.title: The Long Dark Outbound
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. Against protocol, she takes the station's survey skiff toward the coordinates, leaving the garden on automated care. Emotional beat: fear of the open dark versus the pull of being needed by someone, finally.

chapters.title: Perpetua
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. She finds the second ark: scarred, drifting, its hull marked with the same Meridian script. Ten thousand cryopods, power failing. Emotional beat: awe collapsing into horror—the Conclave didn't lose these people; they abandoned them.

chapters.title: The Voice in the Pods
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. She revives one pod briefly—an old woman, Sefa, who wakes just long enough to explain: the Perpetua carried dissidents and the 'genetically redundant.' Emotional beat: grief and fury; Gideon realizes her garden was built with their confiscated resources.

chapters.title: Sefa's Testament
chapters.summary: Sefa's POV, recorded log. The history of the Collapse, the schism, and how the Conclave wrote half of humanity out of existence. Emotional beat: dignified sorrow; a civilization's confession delivered from a deathbed of ice.

chapters.title: Return to Order
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. She returns to the Verdance and files nothing, telling herself she'll decide slowly—but the skiff's flight logs have already auto-reported. Emotional beat: paranoia blooming; the walls of her invisibility closing in.

chapters.title: The Enforcer Arrives
chapters.summary: Dual POV opening on Inspector Callum Reyes, Conclave Justice Division, arriving under cover of a routine resupply. He is courteous, thorough, and lying about why he came. Emotional beat: polite menace; two people circling the same secret.

chapters.title: Tea and Interrogation
chapters.summary: Alternating Gideon/Reyes POV. Over dinner, Reyes probes her records while Gideon performs innocence. Each recognizes the other's performance. Emotional beat: cat-and-mouse intimacy; unexpected mutual respect forming inside mutual deception.

chapters.title: Root Systems
chapters.summary: Reyes's POV. Alone, he reviews Gideon's file and finds his own name flagged in a Conclave sub-routine—he was sent not to investigate but to be implicated if things go wrong. Emotional beat: disillusionment; the law he serves is using him as a fuse.

chapters.title: The Garden Remembers
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. She discovers the Verdance's gene-bank contains Perpetua-era cultivars—proof the Conclave harvested the abandoned ark. Emotional beat: betrayal made botanical; every plant she loved is evidence of a crime.

chapters.title: A Bargain in the Greenhouse
chapters.summary: Gideon and Reyes POV. Reyes confronts her; instead of arresting her, he proposes they wake the Perpetua quietly and blame a systems failure. Emotional beat: dangerous hope; duty cracking down the middle for both of them.

chapters.title: Conclave Static
chapters.summary: Reyes's POV. His encrypted report triggers an automated response: a Justice cutter is inbound, six weeks out, with authority to sterilize the site. Emotional beat: cold panic; the clock starts.

chapters.title: Six Weeks
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. She and Reyes plan: revive the Perpetua's crew, move the ark behind the moon, and make the Verdance look like the only story. Emotional beat: purpose replacing fear; loneliness ending in partnership.

chapters.title: Waking the First Hundred
chapters.summary: Ensemble POV via Gideon's log entries. The first revival wave: disoriented dissidents, engineers, a Meridian linguist named Iyo who can read the ark's locked systems. Emotional beat: fragile joy; strangers learning to trust a stranger's stranger.

chapters.title: Iyo's Key
chapters.summary: Iyo's POV. She unlocks the Perpetua's command deck and finds the Conclave's original extermination order, signed generations ago—and countersigned by the current First Minister's ancestor. Emotional beat: righteous anger hardening into resolve.

chapters.title: What Love Costs
chapters.summary: Gideon and Reyes POV, alternating intimate scenes. They admit feelings neither planned for, knowing one of them may not survive the coming weeks. Emotional beat: tenderness under sentence; love chosen precisely because time is short.

chapters.title: The Cutter Comes Early
chapters.summary: Multiple POV. The Justice cutter arrives three weeks ahead of schedule, having intercepted a partial transmission. Emotional beat: plan shattered; improvisation becomes survival.

chapters.title: Hide the Ark, Burn the Truth
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. Desperate maneuvers: the Perpetua burns toward lunar shadow while Gideon falsifies Verdance logs to draw the cutter's fire. Emotional beat: self-erasure; she destroys her own life's record to save strangers.

chapters.title: Reyes Stands in the Door
chapters.summary: Reyes's POV. Boarded by Justice marines, Reyes claims sole responsibility, buying time but sealing his own arrest. Emotional beat: sacrifice without drama; a good man choosing the consequences he always knew were coming.

chapters.title: Interrogation of the Loyalist
chapters.summary: Reyes's POV aboard the cutter. He refuses to give up the Perpetua even under threat of treason charges. Emotional beat: quiet defiance; justice and law visibly parting ways.

chapters.title: Gideon Alone Again
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. With Reyes taken and the ark hidden, she faces the choice the blurb promised: which ark gets the remaining power and wake priority. Emotional beat: crushing weight of a decision no one person should hold.

chapters.title: The Arithmetic of Souls
chapters.summary: Gideon and council-of-woken POV. The Perpetua's leaders argue for seizing both arks' resources by force; Gideon argues for sharing. Emotional beat: moral friction; she must defend mercy to people with every reason to hate.

chapters.title: Sefa Wakes Fully
chapters.summary: Sefa's POV. Revived completely, the old woman becomes the movement's conscience, backing Gideon against her own people's hawks. Emotional beat: intergenerational trust; the past blessing the future.

chapters.title: Broadcast Zero
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. She hijacks the Verdance beacon to transmit the extermination order and the Perpetua's existence to both arks and the cutter's crew. Emotional beat: terrifying liberation; the truth as a weapon that cannot be recalled.

chapters.title: Fracture on the Cutter
chapters.summary: Crew POV (marine Sergeant Okafor). Reyes's trial-mate crew splits; some arrest him, some mutiny after hearing Broadcast Zero. Emotional beat: institutional collapse from within; the law losing its monopoly on legitimacy.

chapters.title: The First Minister's Silence
chapters.summary: Antagonist POV: First Minister Adeyemi receives word and orders the Verdance destroyed rather than risk exposure. Emotional beat: banal evil; corruption executing itself through calm procedure.

chapters.title: Orbital Fire
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. Conclave weapons target the Verdance. Gideon stays to manually steer the barrage away from the Perpetua's descent corridor. Emotional beat: terror transfigured into devotion; the gardener defending her garden by becoming its shield.

chapters.title: Descent
chapters.summary: Perpetua landing-party POV. The ark's shuttles burn atmosphere toward the surface Gideon terraformed for them. Emotional beat: exodus and homecoming fused; the garden's true purpose fulfilled at last.

chapters.title: The Burning Green
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV, climax. Wounded, she holds the beam-steering console as the Verdance breaks apart around her, broadcasting until the last second. Emotional beat: transcendence through sacrifice; she dies-to-herself among the living things she raised.

chapters.title: Aftermath in the Ash Rows
chapters.summary: Iyo's POV. Survivors find Gideon alive in a sealed root cellar beneath the greenhouse, barely breathing, cradling seed vaults. Emotional beat: resurrection; what she saved saves her.

chapters.title: Trial of Callum Reyes
chapters.summary: Reyes's POV. Brought before a Conclave tribunal now facing open mutiny, Reyes testifies; Okafor and half the cutter's crew stand with him. Emotional beat: justice outside the law taking institutional form.

chapters.title: The Conclave Breaks
chapters.summary: Multi-POV montage. Broadcast Zero spreads through colonial networks; Adeyemi's government fractures; regional councils side with the Perpetua. Emotional beat: revolution as cascade, not battle.

chapters.title: Two Arks, One World
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV, recovering. Negotiations between the original colonists' descendants and the Perpetua's people; Gideon's shared-garden plan becomes the founding charter. Emotional beat: reconciliation earned, not given.

chapters.title: First Planting
chapters.summary: Ensemble POV. The merged community plants the first open-field crops on the surface, mixing both arks' seed lines. Emotional beat: communal joy; grief composted into growth.

chapters.title: Reyes's Choice
chapters.summary: Reyes and Gideon POV. Offered a seat in the new provisional government, Reyes declines to stay near Gideon and help build something local and real. Emotional beat: love choosing presence over power.

chapters.title: The New Beacon
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. The rebuilt station's beacon is repurposed: not a summons for the Conclave, but a welcome signal for any other forgotten ships still drifting. Emotional beat: vigilance transformed into hospitality.

chapters.title: Wren and the Colony
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV, coda. Years later, children born planet-side call her 'Wren' for the small bird she released from the ruined station. She tends the garden for people already here. Emotional beat: peace; the woman who tended a garden for the unborn now watches the born thrive in it.
